title: Good right homotopies and homotopy extension along a cofibration
statement:
Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category as in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. A path object for an object $Z$ consists of maps $Z\xrightarrow{\iota}P\xrightarrow{(p_0,p_1)}Z\times Z$ whose composite is the diagonal and with $\iota$ a weak equivalence. It is good if $(p_0,p_1)$ is a fibration. A right homotopy from maps $a,b:T\to Z$ is a map $H:T\to P$ for some path object satisfying $p_0H=a$ and $p_1H=b$.

(a) Whenever a right homotopy from $a$ to $b$ exists, it can be represented using a good path object, with the same endpoint maps $a,b$.

(b) Suppose $Z$ is fibrant, $P$ is a good path object for $Z$, $H:T\to P$ is a specified right homotopy from $a$ to $b$, $i:T\to U$ is a cofibration, and $l_0:U\to Z$ satisfies $l_0i=a$. There are $l_1:U\to Z$ and a right homotopy $\widetilde H:U\to P$ from $l_0$ to $l_1$ such that $\widetilde H i=H$. In particular $l_1i=b$. No cofibrancy hypothesis on $T$ or $U$ is required.
